darkcraft.cap.1.p1: If you are reading this, you have climbed the Ascent Tower. Few try. None come down the same as they went up. Sit, and listen to an old man.
darkcraft.cap.1.p2: My name is Aldous, and I was the king's chronicler. I write so that someone remembers what Valdrenn was: the jewel of the kingdom, its towers touching the clouds, its rivers singing through every street.
darkcraft.cap.1.p3: Our king, Corvin, loved Queen Isolde more than his own crown. When the grey fever began to take her, no healer, no prayer and no offering could save her.
darkcraft.cap.1.p4: On a moonless night the king went down alone beneath the storm and spoke with the Nameless Shadow. He offered a bargain: the queen's life... in exchange for everything else.
darkcraft.cap.1.p5: The Shadow agreed. That very night the whole kingdom was torn from the earth and raised into the sky. Since then its rivers fall into the void, and the storm has not ceased for a single day.
darkcraft.cap.1.p6: No one died. It was worse. Soldiers, servants and nobles were left hollow, without souls, and they still walk these halls. Expect no mercy from them: they no longer remember their names.
darkcraft.cap.1.p7: Two guardians keep the curse alive: the King, who still waits in his Throne Hall, and Sir Gavran, his sworn knight, who keeps watch at the very top of the Crown Tree.
darkcraft.cap.1.p8:
Slay them both and perhaps the storm will end. I will not tell you how; I only write. My next page awaits you where the water still sings, beside the Great Fountain.

- A.
darkcraft.cap.2.p1: The queen used to sit here every evening. She said the murmur of this fountain reminded her of her homeland, across the sea.
darkcraft.cap.2.p2: When the king returned from the storm, she opened her eyes. We celebrated like madmen. For three days there was music in the courtyards and wine in every cellar.
darkcraft.cap.2.p3: On the fourth day the servants stopped eating. On the fifth, their eyes turned grey as ash. The bells rang on their own before dawn, with no one pulling the ropes.
darkcraft.cap.2.p4: Sir Gavran ordered the gates shut so that no one could flee or enter. He swore he would protect the king even if the whole world burned. He kept that oath far too well.
darkcraft.cap.2.p5: One by one, my people emptied. I watched them carry on with their duties: sweeping empty halls, serving tables with no guests, standing guard before no one.
darkcraft.cap.2.p6: I did not change. I do not know if it is a gift or a punishment from the Shadow. Perhaps it needs someone to remember everything... or someone to tell it to you.
darkcraft.cap.2.p7:
Seek the King. He still sits upon his throne, waiting for a queen who never comes. When he falls, you will find my third page beside him.

- A.
darkcraft.cap.3.p1: So the King has fallen. May the light, if any is left, have mercy on him.
darkcraft.cap.3.p2: You must know the truth. The Shadow did not give the queen back: it gave back something wearing her face. Isolde awoke, but her laughter was no longer her own.
darkcraft.cap.3.p3: Corvin knew it from the first kiss. Even so, he kept loving her. Every night he sat on that throne, waiting for the true Isolde to walk through the door.
darkcraft.cap.3.p4: The bargain had another price: the crown. As long as Corvin wore it, the Shadow would keep one foot in this world. That is why it cracked, and why he never took it off.
darkcraft.cap.3.p5: Now the crown is broken for good. The storm roars weaker, can you hear it? But it is not enough. Someone still holds the oath.
darkcraft.cap.3.p6: When the queen stopped being the queen, Bishop Merrow sealed her beneath the altar of the cathedral. Since then no one dares to enter the nave.
darkcraft.cap.3.p7:
Go to the cathedral. My fourth page waits at the foot of the altar. And pay no heed to the voices you hear inside.

- A.
darkcraft.cap.4.p1: This cathedral was the most beautiful thing Valdrenn ever raised. Now its pews wait only for the dead.
darkcraft.cap.4.p2: Bishop Merrow sealed the queen beneath this altar with seven locks and seven prayers. They say you can still hear her singing, very softly, whenever lightning strikes.
darkcraft.cap.4.p3: On the night they sealed her, the earth shook and a tree burst from the heart of the keep. It grew to the sky in a single night, splitting stone and beams on its way.
darkcraft.cap.4.p4: We called it the Crown Tree. Its roots drink from the Shadow, and its crown holds the last piece of the bargain: the oath of Sir Gavran.
darkcraft.cap.4.p5: Gavran climbed its branches and never came down. They say he has grown with the tree, that he now stands as tall as three men, and that his armour has melted into his skin.
darkcraft.cap.4.p6: While he lives, the storm will not leave. He will let no one reach the top. Bring the finest steel you can find, and more courage than you think you have.
darkcraft.cap.4.p7:
Climb the Crown Tree to its highest hall. If you prevail, my last page will lie at his feet.

- A.
darkcraft.cap.5.p1: Sir Gavran has fallen. His oath is broken, and with it breaks whatever bound the Shadow to these stones.
darkcraft.cap.5.p2: Thank you. For a hundred years no one has read me. I can feel the ink slipping from my fingers; I think at last I will be able to rest.
darkcraft.cap.5.p3: But listen well: the Shadow does not live here. This kingdom was only its door. It waits much further away, where the storm is born.
darkcraft.cap.5.p4: Gavran kept a key that is not made of iron, but of bone. Use it, and it will show you the way to fortresses that float beyond the clouds.
darkcraft.cap.5.p5: They say that behind them rises a mountain that touches the stars, and a castle where the bonfires of the fallen burn. There one rests... and from there one returns.
darkcraft.cap.5.p6: I can no longer go with you. Whatever comes now is yours alone. Seek, fight, fall and rise again. No one else will write your story.
darkcraft.cap.5.p7:
Here ends the chronicle of Valdrenn. May your steel never dull and your fire never fade.

- Aldous, last chronicler of the king.

darkcraft.narracion.1.1: In the days of the Broken Crown, Valdrenn was the jewel of the kingdom.
darkcraft.narracion.1.2: Its towers touched the clouds, and its rivers sang through every street.
darkcraft.narracion.1.3: But Queen Isolde fell ill, and no healer, no prayer, could save her.
darkcraft.narracion.1.4: So King Corvin went down beneath the storm... and made a pact with the Nameless Shadow.
darkcraft.narracion.1.6: That night, the kingdom was torn from the earth, and its rivers began to fall into the void.
darkcraft.narracion.1.7: The people of Valdrenn did not die. They were hollowed... and they still walk these halls.
darkcraft.narracion.1.8: From the heart of the keep grew the Crown Tree, and at its peak, a sworn knight keeps his watch.
darkcraft.narracion.1.9: The King still waits upon his throne. The Knight still guards the sky.
darkcraft.narracion.1.10: Slay them both... and perhaps, at last, the storm will end.
darkcraft.narracion.5.1: Sir Gavran has fallen. His oath is broken... and with it, the chain that bound the Shadow to these stones.
darkcraft.narracion.5.2: Thank you. For a hundred years, no one has read my words.
darkcraft.narracion.5.3: I can feel the ink slipping from my fingers. I think, at last, I may rest.
darkcraft.narracion.5.4: But listen well. The Shadow does not live here. This kingdom was only its door.
darkcraft.narracion.5.5: It waits much farther away... where the storm is born.
darkcraft.narracion.5.6: Gavran kept a key that is not made of iron, but of bone.
darkcraft.narracion.5.7: Use it, and it will show you the way to fortresses that float beyond the clouds.
darkcraft.narracion.5.8: Beyond them, they say, rises a mountain that touches the stars... where the bonfires of the fallen burn.
darkcraft.narracion.5.9: I cannot walk with you any longer. What comes next is yours.
darkcraft.narracion.5.10: Search. Fight. Fall... and rise again. No one else will write your story.
darkcraft.narracion.5.11: Here ends the chronicle of Valdrenn. May your steel never dull... and your fire never fade.
darkcraft.rey.voz.1: At last... a visitor. I have waited so long upon this throne.
darkcraft.rey.voz.2: The Shadow promised me a kingdom without end. And you have come to take it from me?
darkcraft.rey.voz.3: Then kneel before your king... or die standing!
darkcraft.rey.voz.4: Enough! Burn... burn with my kingdom!
darkcraft.rey.voz.5: If my kingdom must fall, you will fall with me... into the fire!
darkcraft.rey.voz.6: The crown... was never mine to keep...
darkcraft.rey.voz.8: Is that all? My guards fought better than you.
darkcraft.rey.voz.9: Feel the fire that devoured my city!
darkcraft.rey.voz.10: No more robes. No more court. Look upon what the fire made of me!
darkcraft.gavran.voz.1: So... the King is dead. I felt it in the roots, the moment his heart stopped.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.2: He was my king. My friend. And a fool who sold us all to the Shadow.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.3: But I swore an oath... and an oath does not die with the man who heard it.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.4: Draw your blade. Let us end this... as knights.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.7: Rise, my squires. Your oath is not yet fulfilled.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.8: Is this the blade that felled my king?
darkcraft.gavran.voz.9: You fight well. It changes nothing.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.10: Rest now. The tree will keep you.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.11: Enough! Tree of the Crown... take what is left of me!
darkcraft.gavran.voz.13: The roots run deeper than your courage.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.14: Nowhere in this hall is beyond my reach!
darkcraft.gavran.voz.15: The floor is mine. Climb... or be taken.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.16: The heart... you found the heart...
darkcraft.gavran.voz.17: Well fought... The oath is broken... at last.
darkcraft.gavran.voz.18: Corvin, my friend... I kept my word. Let the tree... bloom.

darkcraft.perdido.1.p1:
Rye flour.
Coarse salt.
Three dozen black candles for the castle (black? the steward would not say why).
Honey for the Queen.
darkcraft.perdido.1.p2:
Note: since she came back, the Queen eats no bread. No honey. Nothing.

The candles, though, are gone every night.
darkcraft.perdido.2.p1: Mother: do not come to the city for the feast. The Queen has returned and everyone celebrates, but I walk the night watch and I hear her laughing in the gardens.
darkcraft.perdido.2.p2:
It is not her laugh. She used to laugh like little bells. Now it sounds like the wind when it gets into the crypts.

The captain says I must not speak of it. With love,
Joren.
darkcraft.perdido.3.p1:
Brothers and sisters: some pacts are signed in ink, and some are signed with what we love most. The King signed the second kind.

The Shadow does not give back: it lends.
darkcraft.perdido.3.p2: And what it lends, it takes back with interest. Pray for Corvin. Pray for Isolde, if anything of her is left to hear our prayers.
darkcraft.perdido.3.p3: (The bishop never spoke these words. He was found the next morning sitting in his chair, staring north, toward the clouds.)
darkcraft.perdido.4.p1: Today I saw the Queen in the garden. It was night, there was a moon and I was at the window. The Queen was standing very still by the fountain.
darkcraft.perdido.4.p2:
The statues had shadows. The trees had shadows.

The Queen did not.

Mum says I dreamed it. I did not dream it.
darkcraft.perdido.5.p1: Ser Gavran brought me a long white bone. It was not from a cow or a horse. He asked me to make a key from it, and to ask no questions.
darkcraft.perdido.5.p2: Working it was like carving ice that never melts. When I finished, the key was warm. Ser Gavran said it opened a door beyond the clouds, many leagues from here.
darkcraft.perdido.5.p3:
He also said he hoped no one would ever have to use it.

He said it the way one prays.
darkcraft.perdido.6.p1:
I swear to guard the gate of the sky.
I swear to open it to none who lacks the bone key.
I swear not to sleep.
I swear not to die.
darkcraft.perdido.6.p2:
(Below, in another hand:)

We kept all four.
The last one we did not choose.
darkcraft.perdido.7.p1:
Day 40. The stones rise on their own when night falls. No one pushes them. The King says it is the Shadow, helping us.

I never asked for help.
darkcraft.perdido.7.p2: Day 77. We are above the clouds now. From here you cannot see Valdrenn, but you can hear its storm, far away, like a drum.
darkcraft.perdido.7.p3:
Day 103. They brought bones for the walls. Many. They say they are animal bones.

I have buried animals all my life and never seen bones like these.
darkcraft.perdido.8.p1: If anyone reads this, I am no longer the one guarding the gate. I feel the cold rising through my legs, my chest. The others no longer speak: they only growl inside their helms.
darkcraft.perdido.8.p2:
Do not come near us. Do not ask for mercy: we will no longer know how to give it.

If you have the key, climb quickly. And forgive us.
darkcraft.perdido.9.p1:
Dearest Corvin: you asked me to come back, and I came back.

Why will you no longer look me in the eyes?
darkcraft.perdido.9.p2: It is pleasant up here. It is cold and no one weeps. The Shadow says it will soon open the door at the very top, and then all of Valdrenn will be like me.
darkcraft.perdido.9.p3:
Calm. Silent. Eternal.

Isn't that what you wanted?
darkcraft.perdido.10.p1: At the very top of the tower stands an arch that leads nowhere. The stone is cold even in full sun.
darkcraft.perdido.10.p2: It does not open to strength or fire. It answers to what it remembers: the bone of an oath, the light of diamonds, the metal of the underworld.
darkcraft.perdido.10.p3:
Whoever opens it will see the other side. Whoever crosses it will never be the same.

I do not intend to find out.
darkcraft.perdido.11.p1:
Day watch: everyone.
Night watch: everyone.
Relief: never.

Whoever falls asleep on the wall, let him not wake.
darkcraft.perdido.12.p1:
To whoever can still read:

The Grey Heron will not sail again. The Captain has ordered her taken apart, and what he orders in Brumavela is still done.
darkcraft.perdido.12.p2: The sail, to the warehouse on the quay. The tavern keeper kept the helm, for what the crew owes her. The friars guard the new mast in the crypt: it is blessed wood.
darkcraft.perdido.12.p3:
Of the anchor I only know they lowered poor Tobias with it down the Ledge, and the chain is still there.

And the heart he carried up to the lighthouse himself. He says that while it burns, our own will find the way back.
darkcraft.perdido.13.p1:
Nobody pays any more. They sit, stare at the mug and do not drink. Yesterday I spoke to young Hobb and it took him a long while to turn his head.

There was no one behind his eyes.
darkcraft.perdido.13.p2:
They say it is the mist, rising from the sea of clouds ever since the King of Valdrenn did what he did.

I have hung the Heron's helm behind the bar. If they come for it, let them. I am not waiting for anyone.
darkcraft.perdido.14.p1: Brumavela had three founders, and three bells bear their names: the Fisherman's looks to the quay, the Weaver's to the north and the Keeper's to his lighthouse.
darkcraft.perdido.14.p2:
When the last of us falls silent, let them ring in the order in which the founders left, and the crypt will open to make room for us.

Their gravestones do not lie: they stand at the foot of the chapel.
darkcraft.perdido.15.autor: Tobias, topman of the Grey Heron
darkcraft.perdido.15.p1: Lena: the Captain says the island is slipping away, that the mist is dragging it, and he means to moor it to the clouds with the Heron's anchor. Tomorrow I go down the Ledge with it.
darkcraft.perdido.15.p2:
Do not laugh. You have not seen the ship's heart beat: a storm stone, blue, that sings very softly. That is what makes the Heron fly. That is how we will get back to Valdrenn.

Keep my supper for me.
darkcraft.perdido.16.autor: Edrik Maroll, captain of the Grey Heron
darkcraft.perdido.16.p1: I took the Heron apart with my own hands. If no one can leave, no one will carry this to another island. So I told myself.
darkcraft.perdido.16.p2:
I carried the heart up to the lighthouse. While it burns, those who fell into the sea of clouds will find their way home.

And they did. God help us: they did.
darkcraft.perdido.16.p3:
They come up from the quay every night, dripping mist, and they do not know me. I no longer know myself.

Whoever reads this: do not take the heart. Or take it, and take us with you.
darkcraft.perdido.17.autor: Oswin, last watchman of the dome
darkcraft.perdido.17.p1: There were twelve of us watchmen beneath the dome. We kept the garden, Maester Velan's tower and, by night, in turns, the door at the very top. No one ever told us what it guarded.
darkcraft.perdido.17.p2:
When the sky turned red, the other eleven went up to look. They never came down. Now they walk the garden with burning eyes and fade away if you look at them.

I hid down here, beneath the fountain.
darkcraft.perdido.17.p3:
The maester's treasure is not in the armoury. It lies behind the wall that is no wall: in the cellar, in the west guardroom. Strike it well and it crumbles like ash.

May he forgive me. No one needs it now.
darkcraft.perdido.18.p1: I have rung the bell of Velmor for as long as I can remember: for mass, for fire, for the dead. When the sky turned red over the heart of the land, I rang it for fire. No one came.
darkcraft.perdido.18.p2: They did not die. They stayed. The miller's wife is still in her field, reaping what no longer grows; the smith strikes a cold anvil; no one drinks in the tavern. We broke the bridge so that nothing would come. It made no difference: what withers us does not travel by road.
darkcraft.perdido.18.p3:
They are walking ash, and ash thirsts for whatever still breathes. If you hear my bell, it is not mass: it means someone living has entered Velmor, and they know it.

I hear it now from the inside too.
darkcraft.perdido.19.autor: Master Odran, hangman of the Grove
darkcraft.perdido.19.p1: Year of the red sky. Hanged in the Grove: two horse thieves, the miller of Brezal (stolen grain), three deserters of the Oath and a woman who said the Shadow spoke to her in dreams. All as the law commands.
darkcraft.perdido.19.p2: They bring no one anymore: there is no one left to judge. But the ropes creak all the same, and this morning the miller had his eyes open. He was watching me. I cut two of them down and they walked off among the trees.
darkcraft.perdido.19.p3:
If you read this, cut no rope and do not walk beneath the branches. I am staying with them. Someone has to keep the count... and the tree still has room.

O.
darkcraft.perdido.20.autor: Sister Ilse, of the chapel on the stilts
darkcraft.perdido.20.p1: Since the sky turned red, the water of the lagoon is black. The fish float belly up and no one eats them. The nets come up full of something that is not fish. This morning I blessed the water three times; three times it darkened again.
darkcraft.perdido.20.p2: Those who drown do not stay at the bottom. They rise to the surface bloated, face down, and one night they stand up. At night there are green lights among the reeds: the children follow them and never come back. Do not follow the lights.
darkcraft.perdido.20.p3:
The ferryman still crosses the lagoon, though there is no one left to carry. I hear him rowing beneath the chapel. Today he knocked at the door. I pray with the water up to my knees: if you read this, do not board his boat.

Sr. Ilse
darkcraft.perdido.21.titulo: What I Saw from the Gatehouse
darkcraft.perdido.21.autor: Brother Wendel, gatekeeper of the Frostbound Monastery
darkcraft.perdido.21.p1: For forty winters I have opened this gate to the pilgrims. They climbed waist-deep in snow to pray with us at the Frost. Since the sky turned red no one comes up anymore... and those who were already on the road never arrived.
darkcraft.perdido.21.p2: The cold came into the church during vespers. Father Prior bade us keep praying: "the Lord does not forsake His own". We prayed until we could no longer move. The brothers are still there, kneeling in the pews, frost in their beards. Sometimes I hear them whisper.
darkcraft.perdido.21.p3:
Abbot Hrodric did not pray with us. He climbed to the summit to beg the cold to spare us, and the cold answered him. I have seen him come down at night, taller than the tower, wearing a mitre of ice. If you read this, do not climb to the summit. And never kneel in this house.

Br. Wendel
darkcraft.perdido.22.titulo: The Watch of the West Gate
darkcraft.perdido.22.autor: Sergeant Brannoc, of the Oath Guard
darkcraft.perdido.22.p1: Night of the red sky. The Constable orders the West Gate shut: no one comes in, no one goes out. The bridge watch had not yet come back. We lowered the portcullis with them calling from the other side. I write that down too.
darkcraft.perdido.22.p2: Across the river the palace was burning. That fire did not catch on the roofs: it fell from the sky, red, and water would not put it out. Those inside threw themselves against the gate to get out. We held it. That is what we swore.
darkcraft.perdido.22.p3:
"I swear to guard the gate. I swear not to sleep. I swear not to die."

We sleep no more. We burn without burning away and we keep to the wall-walk. The Constable says the gate is still shut. If you read this, you come from outside... and no one passes this gate.

Sgt. Brannoc
darkcraft.perdido.23.autor: Ser Halvard, Constable of the Oath
darkcraft.perdido.23.p1: To the Oath Guard, at every gate. Tonight the sky burns and fire falls upon the palace. If it leaves these walls, the whole kingdom will burn. Shut the gates. No one comes in and no one goes out: not the people, not the guard, not I.
darkcraft.perdido.23.p2: I hear the people in the streets. They beat on the portcullis, they call me by my name. I hold the order. That is what we swore: to guard the gate, not to sleep, not to die. I swore it first, here, before the stone. If I am wrong, let the sky judge me... not them.
darkcraft.perdido.23.p3:
If someone reads this, my gate has opened and I guard it no more. Then there is no oath left to keep. Open the gates. Let them go home.

Ser Halvard, Constable of the Oath
darkcraft.perdido.24.autor: Master Orlen, Keeper of the Great Library
darkcraft.perdido.24.p1: Night of the red sky. Rector Ysolde has gone up to the observatory with her masters to read the fire that falls. She says it is not fire: it is writing. Those of us below she has bidden to keep studying and not go out. The custodians have chained the tomes.
darkcraft.perdido.24.p2: The apprentices sleep no more. They read without turning the page; if you speak to them, they answer with the line in front of them. The vein sings beneath the cloister. No one comes down from the observatory, but the Rector's light still burns.
darkcraft.perdido.24.p3:
If you are reading this, do not read it aloud: what they read stays with you. To the east, in the observatory, the Rector is still reading the sky... and the sky is reading her.

Master Orlen, Keeper of the Great Library
darkcraft.perdido.25.p1: Night of the red sky, third hour. The fire falling on the capital is not fire: it is lines. They join stars that were on no chart. I have sent my masters to their lecterns and closed the door with the seal. No one goes down until we have read it all.
darkcraft.perdido.25.p2: Sixth hour. I can read it now. It is a name, written with the stars of the whole sky, and it is no one's name who was ever born. The more I read it, the clearer it shows. My masters no longer speak: they copy. I cannot take my eye from the telescope.
darkcraft.perdido.25.p3:
I do not know the hour. This night does not end. It is no longer I who read: something reads me, line by line, from above. If anyone finds these pages, do not look through the telescope. And if you see me still standing before it, make me lower my eyes. Please.

Ysolde
darkcraft.perdido.26.autor: Tomé, keeper of the Stranded Harbour's light
darkcraft.perdido.26.p1: Night of the red sky. At high tide the sea went away. It did not ebb: it went, all at once, as if someone had drunk it. The boats were left lying on the sand, and the whale that followed the fleet was stranded in the middle of the bay.
darkcraft.perdido.26.p2: At dawn everyone went down onto the sand to gather the fish, the shells, whatever the sea had left. I shouted from the gallery for them to come up. They did not. The sea did not come back, and the salt began to creep up their legs. Now they are still down there, at work.
darkcraft.perdido.26.p3:
I have lit the lighthouse with cold fire: it is the only thing that still burns. If anyone reads this, do not go down into the bay. And do not go north, to the Ribcage: old Brann the whaler is still there, harpooning a whale that has long been gone.

Tomé, keeper of the Stranded Harbour's light
darkcraft.perdido.27.autor: Brann, harpooner of the Stranded Harbour
darkcraft.perdido.27.p1: First day without the sea. The Old One was in range when the water went: I saw her sink into the sand as if the sand were the sea. Forty years after her, and she slips me like that. Her sister whale was stranded here; I have made my home in her ribs.
darkcraft.perdido.27.p2: I no longer know the day. The salt has climbed to my chest and I am no longer hungry. Every night I hear her singing under the sand, and in the morning I see her spout out there, to the east. I have sharpened the harpoon and filled the lantern with oil. When she surfaces, I will be awake.
darkcraft.perdido.27.p3:
If anyone reads this: keep away from the ribs. My boat lies overturned and my men went back to the harbour to mend nets that are no use anymore. I stay. The Old One will surface, and this time she will not slip me. After that, let the tide come back.

Brann
darkcraft.perdido.28.autor: Brother Ulric, hospitaller of the Bridge of the Rift
darkcraft.perdido.28.p1: Since the night of the red sky the pilgrims have not stopped coming. They come from the south, barefoot, to beg forgiveness of the crater. I give them bread and a straw bed, and in the morning I ring the bridge bell for each one who crosses. They used to cross singing.
darkcraft.perdido.28.p2: Today he arrived, at the head of the last procession: Anselm, who calls himself Pontiff. He says the sky took our faith and only blood can buy it back. The pilgrims listen to him with empty eyes. No one slept tonight: all one could hear was the lash.
darkcraft.perdido.28.p3:
He leads them northwest, to the Altar of Blood, beyond the rifts, where the earth is reddest. They come back from there with their faces hooded and their backs laid open, and they no longer cross: they pray. If anyone reads this, do not ring the bell. They come.

Brother Ulric
darkcraft.perdido.29.p1: Brothers: we went to the crater to beg forgiveness and no one answered. For years we prayed to the empty sky. And on the night of the red sky, at last, something answered. It did not say forgiven. It said: give.
darkcraft.perdido.29.p2: So we give. Our backs, so that the sky sees we keep nothing back. Our blood, for the altar, which is always thirsty. Those who doubted left by the southern road; I no longer name them. Those who stayed are no longer afraid: they no longer have anything.
darkcraft.perdido.29.p3:
(in another hand, shaking) Blood is not enough. It is never enough. The altar drinks it and the voice of the crater asks for more. If anyone reads this: the voice does not forgive. It collects. And what it collects it carries to the centre, to the red lake, where it waits.

Anselm
darkcraft.perdido.30.p1: I woke at the bottom of the crater with the mark burning on my chest and a voice in my head. 'You were dead,' it said. 'Break my chains and you shall rest.' I found the nearest chain and began to strike it. I did not know how much the Shadow's iron weighs.
darkcraft.perdido.30.p2: Then others came, one by one, with the same mark and the same promise. We are many now, and the chain is only one. We strike in turns, day and night, though here it is never night. The anchor has not moved a finger's breadth. Our hands no longer hurt: they are no longer ours.
darkcraft.perdido.30.p3:
Today I climbed the chain, link by link, until I saw the citadel up close. There is no door up there: there is a mouth that waits. I came down. I will not climb again, and I will let no one who bears the mark climb it. The voice was wrong. It was never about rest.

Aldric
darkcraft.acertijo.p1: Whoever wishes to open the door at the very top must forge an amulet. I wrote it down in verse, so that only a patient reader would understand.
darkcraft.acertijo.p2:
Two lights that never break
crown the forge,
and between them rests
the Nether's iron.

Below, the bone that keeps
an oath
sleeps between two brothers
of that same iron.
darkcraft.acertijo.p3: If the ink resists you, press the seal below: the book will show you the forge, drawn.
darkcraft.narracion.6.1: So... the marked one has climbed all the way to my door.
darkcraft.narracion.6.2: A king begged me for his queen. A knight gave his soul to keep me out.
darkcraft.narracion.6.4: You forged the amulet with your own hands... and you opened my door.
darkcraft.narracion.6.5: Thank you. I have waited a thousand winters for those hands.
darkcraft.narracion.6.8: Every cloud in this world will burn red... until you stand before me.
darkcraft.narracion.6.9: Beyond this door lie the Withered Lands. Morvain. My lands.
darkcraft.narracion.6.10: Cross, marked one. I will be waiting at the heart of it all.
darkcraft.cap.6.p1: So... the marked one has climbed all the way to my door. A king begged me for his queen. A knight gave his soul to keep me out. They failed. You did not.
darkcraft.cap.6.p2: You forged the amulet with your own hands... and you opened my door. Thank you. I have waited a thousand winters for those hands.
darkcraft.cap.6.p3: Now... look up. The sky remembers my name. Every cloud in this world will burn red... until you stand before me.
darkcraft.cap.6.p4: Beyond this door lie the Withered Lands. Morvain. My lands. Cross, marked one. I will be waiting at the heart of it all. I always wait.

darkcraft.dialogo.guia.1: Another soul the Shadow has dragged back from the dark... You should be dead, marked one. And yet... the fire still answers to you.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.2: I am Maelis. I tend the soul fires, as my sisters did... before Valdrenn fell to its oath.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.3: Rest beside them when you can. The fire mends your flesh and fills your flasks... but the fallen will rise again.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.4: It is older than the kingdom. It feeds on broken oaths... and it hungers for a door. Yours is the hand it chose to open it.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.5: Because it needs you. Each time you fall, it pulls you back... and your echoes stay behind, in a sword of light. Do not lose them twice.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.6: Then give me the echoes you carry. I will weave them into your flesh... and your bones.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.7: May the fire keep you, marked one.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.8: You have returned. Good... the fire was waiting for you.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.9: The king's oath is broken at last. I felt every fire burn brighter... and the Shadow grow hungrier.
darkcraft.dialogo.guia.10: Ser Gavran kept his oath to the very end. Honor him, marked one... few in Valdrenn ever did.
darkcraft.dialogo.combate: This is no time to talk: enemies are near.
darkcraft.dialogo.sin_santuario: That needs a kindled sanctuary nearby.
advancements.darkcraft.maelis.title: Keeper of the Fires
advancements.darkcraft.maelis.descriptio: Speak with Maelis beside a sanctuary
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.1: Hm. Another one crawling out of the dark with a dull blade... The name's Dorvan. I keep the forge of Valdrenn burning, oath or no oath.
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.2: Back again? Show me what you've been swinging.
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.3: Bring me forging stones and echoes, and I'll make that steel sing.
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.4: There. Sharper than the day it was forged. Try not to break it on the first skull.
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.5: You're short on stones, or on echoes. The forge doesn't work for free.
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.6: The king swore an oath to something that should never have heard it. After that... the forge was all I had left to keep my hands from shaking.
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.7: Off you go, then. And keep your guard up.
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.8: That one's as good as it gets. Not even I can push it further.
darkcraft.dialogo.herrero.op.mejorar: I want to upgrade my weapon.
darkcraft.dialogo.mercader.1: Ah, a customer! And a living one, more or less. Kerrick's the name. If it can be carried, I've probably got it.
darkcraft.dialogo.mercader.2: Welcome back, friend! Echoes in your pocket, wares on my cart.
darkcraft.dialogo.mercader.3: A fine choice. Spend it well... or don't, and come buy another.
darkcraft.dialogo.mercader.4: Ah... your purse is lighter than your ambition, friend.
darkcraft.dialogo.mercader.5: The dead don't care much for my prices. The living do. So I stay close to the fires... and closer to my cart.
darkcraft.dialogo.mercader.6: Safe roads, friend. And if you find any... do tell me.

darkcraft.diario.maelis: A hooded woman tends the soul fires. Her name is Maelis... and she says the Shadow chose me.
darkcraft.diario.dorvan: In the training yard, a blacksmith still beats his anvil as if nothing had happened. His name is Dorvan.
darkcraft.diario.kerrick: A merchant with a pack bigger than himself sells by the fires. He says only the living complain about his prices.
darkcraft.diario.mejora: Dorvan tempered my weapon. Sharper than the day it was forged.
darkcraft.diario.mejora_maxima: My weapon cannot get any better. Not even Dorvan himself would know how.
darkcraft.diario.compra: I bought something from Kerrick. Not sure it was a good idea... he looked very pleased.
darkcraft.habilidad.torbellino.desc: A full spin with the weapon: strikes everything around you twice.
darkcraft.habilidad.estocada.desc: Lunge forward with a thrust that pierces everything in its line.
darkcraft.habilidad.grito.desc: A roar that sets the blood aflame: weapons hit 20% harder for 20 seconds.
darkcraft.habilidad.sismo.desc: Leap and slam the ground with all your weight: the shockwave hits and lifts everyone around.
darkcraft.habilidad.paso.desc: A quick shadow step in the direction you move; nothing can touch you while it lasts.
darkcraft.habilidad.llamas.desc: A wide slash wreathed in fire that sets ablaze whoever it hits.
darkcraft.habilidad.escarcha.desc: An icy slash that freezes and slows whoever it hits.
darkcraft.habilidad.relampago.desc: An overhead slash that releases a bolt of lightning straight ahead.
darkcraft.habilidad.sangre.desc: A devastating slash paid for with your own blood.
darkcraft.habilidad.parada.desc: Deflects a blow from the front at the right moment and staggers whoever struck it.
darkcraft.habilidad.sin_vida: Not enough health to pay for the Bloody Slash.
darkcraft.forja.nada_cenizas: You carry no weapon that accepts ashes (named weapons have their own arts).
darkcraft.forja.sin_cenizas: You carry no Ashes of War.
darkcraft.forja.no_vale: That ash doesn't suit this weapon.
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.ceniza_aplicar: An ash fuses into a weapon
advancements.darkcraft.ceniza.title: Ashes of War
advancements.darkcraft.ceniza.descriptio: Put an Ash of War on a weapon at Dorvan's forge
advancements.darkcraft.parada.title: At the Perfect Moment
advancements.darkcraft.parada.descriptio: Deflect a blow with a parry
darkcraft.diario.ceniza: Dorvan fused an Ash of War into my weapon. It can do things it couldn't before.
darkcraft.diario.parada: I deflected a blow at the perfect moment. My attacker was left reeling.
darkcraft.menu.historia.bloqueado: You haven't found this chapter yet. Its chest awaits you somewhere in Valdrenn.

darkcraft.opciones.sonido.desc: The volume of everything and the sound device.
darkcraft.opciones.graficos.desc: Render distance, quality, particles, fullscreen... (with Embeddium, its own options).
darkcraft.opciones.controles.desc: The mouse, jumping and sneaking, and every key.
darkcraft.opciones.chat.desc: How the chat looks and behaves.
darkcraft.opciones.accesibilidad.desc: Narrator, subtitles, screen effects and flashes.
darkcraft.opciones.idioma.desc: The game language: the mod's texts and subtitles follow it (voices are in English).
darkcraft.opciones.recursos.desc: The resource packs (textures and sounds) in use, and their order.
